thread:
oncall-bot: [ALERT] SLA breach detected for tenant=Greenleaf (p95 latency > 1200ms) — paging oncall
Samir K: I’m on it. seeing increased tail latency on generation workers that serve zone-us-east-1 for Greenleaf. noisy but pages us due to tenant SLA rule.
Nyla P: Hey — are they actually impacted or is this a metric spike from retry storms? any errors?
Samir K: No 5xx spike, just long token gen times and queueDepth on pool-gpu-7 climbing. looks correlated with requests that have large context lengths (~12k tokens)
Erica M: Can we check prefix cache hit routes? If they’re cold, that explains tail. quick query: `sum by(pool) (queue_depth{pool="pool-gpu-7"})` and `histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(token_latency_bucket[5m]))`
Samir K: Ran quick checks — queue_depth is elevated, and token latency p95 at pool-gpu-7 is ~1600ms. cache_hit_ratio for the tenant is 12% vs baseline 48%.
Ravi S: Greenleaf has a recent migration that increased context length defaults. this could be a tenant config issue — but we still alarmed because we have tenant-specific SLA rule that triggers on p95 > 1.2s. paging is noisy if their workload naturally has long contexts.
Nyla P: For live mitigation: can we abort/short-circuit very long requests from that tenant? we have a soft-limit route override we can push per-tenant to cap max_tokens or enforce streaming chunking.
Samir K: I can push a temporary per-tenant `max_generation_tokens=2048` override via feature flag. will do 2-mins windows and monitor.
oncall-bot: Deployment started: flag-update greenleaf-max-tokens -> 2048 (actor: Samir K)
Samir K: Flag pushed. Also muting the SLA alert for Greenleaf for 10m while we observe `mute_reason=investigating-noise` — will not suppress the incident channel. 
Erica M: Good. While muted, we should add a composite alert to detect real customer impact: create alert `greenleaf-error-or-requests-failed` that fires only on 5xx or user-visible errors (latency alone isn't sufficient). I’ll open the alert change in PagerDuty policies afterwards.
Nyla P: Agree — the current rule is too brittle for tenant-specific profiles. Suggest we: 1) lower sensitivity on pure latency for tenants with historical long contexts, 2) add a composite condition (latency + error-rate) for paging, 3) create a separate dashboard with per-tenant context-length distribution.
Ravi S: Also suggest an autosuggest: when tenant config indicates >50% requests with context>4096, route them to a higher-batch-friendly pool (batching increases per-token throughput). I'll make a runbook note.
Samir K: Observability note — adding a quick dashboard: `tenant:Greenleaf:context-length:hist`, `pool:pool-gpu-7:queue_depth` and `tenant:Greenleaf:cache_hit_ratio`. I’ll pin it to the incident thread.
triage-bot: Incident ticket created: #INC-2026-4827 — impact: degraded latency for Greenleaf, potential SLA breach. assignees: Samir K, Nyla P
Nyla P: Handoff in ~25 minutes to Erica. Samir, can you summarize mitigations you did so Erica can pick up? Also list follow-ups for postmortem.
Samir K: Summary: 1) pushed tenant-level max_tokens override (2048) 2) muted SLA alert for 10m while monitoring 3) verified no spike in 5xx 4) added temporary diagnostic dashboard links
Follow-ups for postmortem: 1) update SLA alerting rules to composite condition (latency+errors) for tenants 2) add per-tenant context-length metric to onboarding checks 3) create an automated routing policy that moves high-context tenants to batch-optimized pools 4) run a 24h retrospective on Greenleaf migration impact
Erica M: I’m taking over. If the override doesn’t reduce p95 in 10m we should rollback (remove override) and instead shift capacity: scale pool-gpu-7 + add a repool for Greenleaf to pool-gpu-batch-2. I’ll prepare scaling commands and a canary re-route.
Samir K: p95 dropped to ~900ms inside 3m of flag. queue_depth dropped by ~40%. looks stable so far.
oncall-bot: [UPDATE] muted alert expired for Greenleaf (mute window ended) — SLA rule back to active.
Nyla P: Since p95 stayed stable post-unmute, propose we change the tenant SLA rule from `p95>1200ms` to `p95>1200ms AND error_rate>0.5%` for tenant-level paging. Also add a new non-paging alarm for `p95>1200ms` labeled `investigate-but-no-page` which notifies SLO channel only.
Erica M: I’ll file a PR to alerting with tests and a preview dashboard. Include a configurable per-tenant sensitivity flag. Also will add a kibana saved search for `tenant:Greenleaf AND level:warn` to track app-level warnings tied to migration.
Ravi S: For immediate noise reduction: create a synthetic check that samples worst-offender tenants and applies a rate-limited notification. We should avoid per-tenant muting by hand long-term.
Samir K: Logged follow-up tasks in #incidents-playbook: `TICKET-4827` with owners. Also noted we should contact Greenleaf CS to warn them of the temporary cap (they may see fewer tokens returned if they rely on very long contexts).
Nyla P: Thanks team. Good mitigation. Erica — I’ll hand off any remaining watch to you. Please update the ticket with the alert PR link and confirm when the new rule is live.
Erica M: Will do. Will also draft a short customer-facing note for CS if we make the change permanent. cc @support
oncall-bot: Incident resolved: SLA breach no longer observed for Greenleaf. Incident closed by Erica M. closed_at=1800001400
Samir K: Nice. Follow-ups captured. Closing my oncall view.
Nyla P: Great job everyone. Postmortem to include timeline + config change diffs + suggested new dashboards. :thumbsup:
Erica M: I'll publish a follow-up summary and link PRs in the ticket tomorrow.
